chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: 'Is the 'awrah (blemish/secret) of a believer upon another believer forbidden?' He said: Yes. I said: Do you mean his lower organs? He said: It is not as you think. It is only the disclosure of his secret.'

key_terms.سَفْل: Lower part, specifically referring to the lower private organs
key_terms.عَوْرَة: Blemish, secret, or private part; here referring to a believer's secrets

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'awrah of a believer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the physical and spiritual dimensions of 'awrah, clarifying that the prohibition against exposing a believer's 'awrah' primarily concerns the dissemination of their secrets (itha'at sirrihi). This interpretation elevates the concept from mere physical modesty to a broader ethical duty of preserving privacy and dignity, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence regarding social conduct. The hadith underscores the sanctity of the believer's inner life, linking it to the preservation of trust (amanah) within the community.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	We were told by Muhammed bin Musa bin Mutawakkil, that he said: We were told by Abdullah bin Ja’far al-Himyari, from Ahmad bin Muhammed, from Hasan bin Mahbub, from Abdullah bin Sinan, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:

Did he say: «The blemish of a believer upon another believer is forbidden»? He said: Yes. I said: Does he mean the two lower organs (of him). He said: It is not as you think. It is only the disclosure of his secret.
